### Draft 1 — Agent-panel keyboard navigation / native agent picker

```markdown
Title: [idea] Keyboard-navigable agent selector (focus Agents panel, j/k + Enter) — like the prefix+w workspace navigator

### idea / problem

The Agents panel (bottom-left sidebar) is only reachable/navigable with the
mouse. Every other unit in herdr has a keyboard path — panes (prefix+h/j/k/l),
workspaces (prefix+w navigator), tabs (prefix+1..9), the goto picker (prefix+g).
Agents have only:

- `next_agent` / `previous_agent` — a blind cycle (and historically couldn't
  cross workspaces, cf #964)
- `focus_agent` indexed (prefix+alt+1..9) — direct, but you must already know
  the number

There's no way to open a **visible, selectable/searchable list of agents and
jump to one** — which is the natural "which agent needs me right now?" workflow,
especially with many agents spread across workspaces.

### requested change

A configurable action that focuses the Agents panel and drives it from the
keyboard, mirroring the prefix+w workspace navigator:

- `focus_agents` (suggested default: `prefix+a`) → move focus into the Agents panel
- once focused: `j`/`k` (or arrows) to move the selection, `Enter` to jump to
  that agent's pane, `Esc` to cancel
- respect the existing `ui.agent_panel_sort` order
- ideally type-to-filter (like the goto picker), since agent names/labels are
  already searchable

Same model as #1009 (closed as "belongs in Discussions"); complements #778 (jump
to first blocked agent) and #599 (repeatable step-through). Cycling and indexed
jump exist already — the missing piece is pick-from-a-visible-list.

### why you want this

Keyboard-first / tmux-migrated users shouldn't need the mouse to answer "which
agent is blocked/done — take me there." A navigable/filterable Agents panel is
the agent-native analog of a sesh/telescope picker and completes herdr's
otherwise-full keyboard story.

Refs: #1009, #778, #599, #964
```

---

### Draft 2 — Git dirty / uncommitted indicator on workspaces

```markdown
Title: [idea] Show a dirty/uncommitted indicator on workspaces (herdr already tracks branch + ahead/behind)

### idea / problem

herdr already surfaces per-workspace git info in the Spaces sidebar — the branch
name (#384) and branch/ahead-behind polling (#353). What it doesn't show is
whether the working tree is **dirty** (uncommitted or untracked changes). That's
often the single most useful at-a-glance signal when juggling many agent
workspaces: "which spaces have unsaved work / changes an agent just made?"

### requested change

Add a dirty indicator to the workspace/Spaces row, e.g.:

- a `*` / `●` / color accent next to the branch when git reports uncommitted or
  untracked changes (`git status --porcelain` non-empty)
- optionally counts (e.g. `+N ~M`) like the existing ahead/behind display
- reuse the existing per-repo git polling (#353) so it's computed in the same
  pass — no extra `git` spawns
- a toggle to disable, consistent with the idle-CPU/polling-cost concerns in #353

If the plugin / custom-status mechanism hinted at in #522 lands first, dirty
state could also be expressed through that — but since git is already
first-class here, a native dirty glyph seems like a small, high-value addition.

### why you want this

With agents editing files across many workspaces, "does this space have
uncommitted changes?" is the question you ask constantly. Branch + ahead/behind
already answer "where am I / am I pushed?"; dirty answers "is there work here to
review/commit?" — the missing third piece of the git-at-a-glance story.

Refs: #384, #353, #522
```

───── #975 ─────
[CLOSED] Bring back current-workspace filtering for the Agents panel
## Summary

Please bring back a project/workspace scope filter for the Agents panel, separate from the new sort mode.

In v0.7.1, the Agents panel workspace/all filter was removed and replaced with `ui.agent_panel_sort = "spaces" | "priority"`. I understand the new global queue model, but for project-focused workflows this is a regression.

## Current behavior

In v0.7.1, the Agents panel always shows all agents across all spaces/workspaces.

`agent_panel_sort = "spaces"` groups/orders agents by space, but it still shows every agent from every project.

This becomes noisy when many projects are open at the same time. Switching to a workspace/project no longer lets me see only the agents for that project.

## Previous behavior / expected behavior

Before this change, the Agents panel had a workspace/all scope concept, e.g. a current-workspace view and an all-workspaces view.

Expected behavior: allow users to choose whether the Agents panel shows:

- only agents in the current workspace/project, or

───── #318 ─────
[CLOSED] feat: sort agents panel by attention priority
## Current behavior

The agents panel lists panes in workspace-iteration order — panes grouped by their workspace, in the order workspaces appear. Status (blocked, done, working, idle) does not affect the order.

A blocked agent at the bottom of the list stays at the bottom until scanned for.

## Proposed change

Add a `sort` option under `[ui.agent_panel]` (or wherever fits the existing config layout):

- `workspace` (default): current behavior, unchanged.
- `priority`: sort by attention priority — blocked > idle/unseen (done) > working > idle/seen > unknown. Stable sort within a status, so workspace order remains a natural tiebreaker.

The priority function `workspace_attention_priority` (`src/ui/sidebar.rs:264`) is already used by `space_aggregate_state` to roll up worktree-group state. Same priority hierarchy, applied to the panel sort.

## Rationale

The panel is the at-a-glance view of all agents. Blocked agents are the highest-signal items — they need a human. Sorting by attention priority makes the panel function as a queue of work instead of a static workspace map. The hierarchy is already encoded in the codebase for the rollup case; this extends the same model to the panel.

Workspaces, tabs, drag-and-drop are unaffected. Opt-in only; default behavior unchanged. With `sort = "priority"`, cycling next/prev agent (`prefix+n`/`prefix+p`) traverses the new order.


───── #304 ─────
[CLOSED] feat: Improve agents sidebar context
### Current behavior

Herdr shows agent state in the sidebar, but multiple running agents can still be hard to tell apart at a glance. The agents list does not make pane context prominent enough, so different agents can look similar even when they are working in different panes.

The sidebar layout is also mostly hardcoded. Adding pane names, working durations, custom status text, or alignment choices as fixed display rules makes the agents sidebar more useful, but it also turns each display preference into another code-level layout decision.

### Requested change

Make the agents sidebar easier to scan by showing clearer per-agent context, starting with pane names so agents can be distinguished more easily.

Also show how long an agent has been working, with blocked approval interruptions treated as part of the same working span when they directly interrupt active work.

Rather than hardcoding each new label, add a small sidebar configuration model so users can control which metadata appears, how it is split across rows, and where right-aligned sidebar content begins. Expose the common configuration in the TUI settings screen instead of requiring manual config edits for normal use.

<img width="1093" height="766" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2baa54a-b265-4434-95f2-7c271dd26d8d" />

### Reason

Herdr is built around managing AI coding agents inside terminal workspaces. When several agents are running at once, the sidebar is the fastest way to understand what is happening without switching panes. Pane names and working durations make that view more operational: users can tell which agent is which and how long each one has been active.

The configurable layout part keeps this from becoming a pile of one-off hardcoded display choices. The default layout can stay familiar, while users who rely heavily on multiple agents can expose the context they need.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-07 10:47:31Z)**_

That's **herdr version skew** between machines — and I can pin down exactly what changed. This machine is on `herdr 0.7.1` and its config has `agent_panel_sort = "priority"`.

## What's going on

Per herdr issue [#975](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/975), the Agents-panel toggle was **redesigned in v0.7.1**:

> "In v0.7.1, the Agents panel workspace/all filter was **removed** and replaced with `ui.agent_panel_sort = "spaces" | "priority"`."

So the two option-sets you're seeing are two different herdr generations:

| Toggle you see | herdr version | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **all / current** | **older** (pre-0.7.1) | *filter by scope* — show every agent vs only the current workspace's agents |
| **grouped / priority** | **0.7.1+** | *sort mode* (`ui.agent_panel_sort`) — `spaces` = grouped by workspace; `priority` = attention order (blocked → done → working → idle, per [#318](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/318)) |

In 0.7.1 the panel **always shows all agents** now; the toggle only changes ordering, not scope. The old "current-workspace only" *filter* was dropped (that's exactly what #975 is asking to bring back).

## Why the machines differ

herdr isn't version-locked across your fleet — this repo installs it **per-OS and install-only**:
- **macOS** → Homebrew (`brew upgrade herdr`)
- **Linux** → self-updating GitHub-release binary (`herdr update`)

`chezmoi apply` never upgrades it (install-only invariant), so whichever machines you haven't upgraded recently are still on the older panel model.

## To unify them

1. **Converge versions** — on the lagging boxes: `herdr update` (Linux) / `brew upgrade herdr` (macOS). Check the spread with `fleet exec 'herdr --version'` if you want to see who's behind.
2. **Optionally pin the sort** — I can add `agent_panel_sort = "priority"` (or `"spaces"`) to the managed `[ui]` table in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` so every 0.7.1+ machine gets the same default. Right now it's a runtime-written value the overlay merely preserves, so it can drift per-host.

One heads-up: if you actually *liked* the **current-workspace-only** view (less noise with many projects open), that was removed in 0.7.1 — #975 is the request to restore it (worth a 👍 in Discussions, same as the ideas we filed).

Want me to pin `agent_panel_sort` in the managed config, and/or run a `fleet exec 'herdr --version'` sweep to see which machines are behind?
